title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's July 1986 manuscript on 'ateliers' (and 'magasins' / 'magasin-atelier', with 'ensembles adonnés' on the previous page). The project is an axiomatic, essentially set-theoretic or lattice-like framework for spaces in which 'lieux' (places, regions) replace points, as an alternative foundation for topology. The page has two parts.

(1) End of a methodological remark, continuing p.121. There he asked whether the notion attached to the 'mal-aimé' object Σ can be recovered by 'inverting the arrows ↠' (subdivisions) in some category built from a relative magasin-atelier (F, ≪). He also noted that for 'boolean' Σ ('ateliers pré-booléens', perhaps the 'fidèles' ones) there is nothing new.
- He now says his structures are, to his conviction, not 'classical'.
- His own 'ordres', 'pseudo-simplicial' and 'topological' variants 'et tutti quanti' are tied to the intuition of lieux replacing points.
- They are, for now, the only ones covering the known cases.

(2) A marked paragraph (vertical bar in the margin). Even for particular ateliers, it would be interesting to see whether Σ admits a direct combinatorial description. This would be in a spirit closer to a 'géométrie des formes' (geometry of shapes), rather than reducing the 'spatial' objects to facts of general topology. Modern reading: he wants an intrinsic combinatorial or poset-theoretic model of the relevant category of shapes or spaces, not one presented via point-set topology. This parallels the moves from spaces to locales, and from topological spaces to simplicial or poset models of homotopy types.

(3) A research plan ('Prochaines choses'):
- Margin, to be done first: perhaps return to relative ateliers and their relations to [ateliers / ensembles adonnés?], to 'close up' the purely set-theoretic aspect.
- a) sub-ateliers and morphisms ('enfin!').
- b) 'ateliers modérés', i.e. tame ateliers.
- c) saturation axioms, and the saturation of an atelier or of a category[-atelier?].

No theorem or proof appears on this page; it is programmatic.
errors: No mathematical claims are asserted, so there is nothing to check. The page openly flags unverified points: on p.121 he had not checked that the localized category is an 'ensemble adonné', nor that it embeds in Σ.
Several words are illegible; the exact referent of 'Σ cas' (perhaps Σ with a subscript) cannot be fixed from this page alone.

ideas.what: Spaces axiomatized via 'lieux' (regions) replacing points; Grothendieck's 'ordres', pseudo-simplicial and topological variants as the only known realizations
ideas.modern_name: point-free topology (locales, frames), mereotopology; poset and simplicial models of spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann, Isbell, Joyal–Tierney, Johnstone (locales); Whitehead / de Laguna (region-based geometry)
ideas.where_published: Theme of 'lieux' versus points echoes topos philosophy in SGA4 and Récoltes et Semailles; the 'ateliers' themselves are unpublished

ideas.what: Wish for a direct combinatorial description of Σ in the spirit of a 'géométrie des formes' rather than general topology
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial or tame models of shape (cf. o-minimal / tame topology, combinatorial models of homotopy types)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's own Esquisse d'un programme (topologie modérée) for the program; van den Dries, Shiota and others for o-minimal realizations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée) and Récoltes et Semailles express similar aims; the specific link to ateliers is not published

ideas.what: Research plan: sub-ateliers and morphisms, 'ateliers modérés', saturation axioms and saturation of an atelier
ideas.modern_name: tame structures; saturation/completion of a lattice-like structure

missed.claim: The plan item 'Ateliers modérés' shows Grothendieck intended his 1986 point-free 'atelier' framework to carry the tame-topology program of the Esquisse (1984). A region-based axiomatics would underlie 'topologie modérée'. This link between tame topology and point-free / region-based foundations is not developed in the o-minimality literature, which stays point-set and model-theoretic.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a point-free or locale-like foundation for tame geometry. That remains a largely open direction, though related questions have been raised in work on o-minimal sheaf theory and in condensed / pyknotic reformulations of topology.

missed.claim: Open question stated by Grothendieck: does the category Σ attached to (particular) ateliers admit a direct combinatorial description, a 'geometry of shapes', independent of general topology? His candidates (ordres, pseudo-simplicial, topological structures) are the only ones known to him.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links to the search for combinatorial models of tame spaces and their homotopy types, e.g. stratified spaces and exit-path categories.

missed.claim: Several planned topics are explicitly listed, which helps date and trace the unpublished atelier theory: relative ateliers, sub-ateliers and morphisms, tame ateliers, and saturation axioms.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical value for reconstructing the never-published 1986 'ateliers' project.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is programmatic with no results. The mildly notable detail is the explicit plan for 'ateliers modérés', which ties the unpublished 1986 point-free 'atelier' theory to the tame-topology program of the Esquisse. Grothendieck's call for a combinatorial 'géométrie des formes' description of Σ points the same way. This connection is little known.
transcription_corrections: Line 2-3: likely 'et mes "ordres", pseudo-simpliciaux, topologiques et tutti quanti, associés' rather than '[?] à mes'.
Line 5-7: plausibly 'qui couvrent tous les [cas] connus pour l'instant, et les seuls connus' rather than 'conservent tous les [?]'.
'Mais même dans le cas des ateliers particuliers' (second word of that line looks like 'ateliers'/'atelier' rather than [?]).
'une description conformément directe' should read 'une description combinatoire directe'.
'dans les [?] spatiales a des faits voulus de topologie générale' is perhaps 'plutôt que [de ramener] les spatios à des faits relevant de topologie générale'; uncertain.
The marginal note 'pour "boucler" l'aspect purement ensembliste - il serait temps !' is attached to item a); 'morphismes' is underlined.
Last line is perhaps 'Saturation d'un atelier, ou d'un atelier-catégorie' (underlined).
